newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mosaic, Kerr up PNG oil stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mosaic, Kerr up PNG oil stake.

text.p: Mosaic Oil NL said it and Kerr McGee Corp have increased their equity in the PPL 163 oil joint venture in Papua New Guinea following the withdrawal of Phillips Petroleum Co.
Mosaic's stake has been raised to 20 percent from 7.7 percent and Kerr McGee's stake to 80 percent from 34.3 percent, as a result of the exit by Phillips, Mosaic said.
Mosaic in a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange that Phillips had wihdrawn for "non-technical reasons" and Mosaic has become the operator.
The Australian newspaper reported on Friday that Phillips walked away from its majority holding after a disagreement with the Papua New Guinea government.
Mosaic said it viewed its increased exposure to the venture as a bonus, given the funds expended by the company in Papua New Guinea so far.
About US$50 million has been spent by the partners, both in PPL 163 and an earlier permit, PPL 94, in roughly the same area of PNG's Western Province, the company said.
"It should be recognised that Phillips Petroleum has made an historic and significant contribution to Papua New Guinea foreland geology," Mosaic said.

"In particular, Phillips Petroleum organised the drilling of Bujon 1 and initiated fluid inclusion research ... and developed oil generation models which have tied oil found in the Bujon well cores with oil generated in the Papuan Fold belt at the Kutubu fields," it said.
Mosaic said it intends along with Kerr McGee to hold discussions with potential farm-in partners.
Well costs associated with three drillable prospects are currently being studied, Mosaic said.
Each poses risks, although if they contain oil, each has the potential to hold 135 million, 300 million and one billion barrels of recoverable oil respectively, Mosaic said.
